newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy April PSBR seen narrowing.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy April PSBR seen narrowing.

text.p: Italy's budget deficit will narrow in April to around 16 trillion lire from 17.5 trillion the previous month and 23.9 trillion in April 1996, economists said.
This would nudge state accounts closer to meeting European monetary union criteria.
The forecasts by five economists for April public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) ranged from 13.5 to 21.0 trillion lire, averaging 16.3 trillion lire.
April's PSBR will gain advantage from petroleum tax receipts carried from the end of March due to the Easter break, a carryover which weighed on March's PSBR, analysts said.
Andrea Marchetti, economist at Credito Italiano expected the April 1997 figure to be helped by lower spending this month on debt servicing and more revenue from mineral taxes.
"The rest are corrections of greater income and controlling of costs due to the budgets," Marchetti said.

BCI economist Moreno Capretti did not expect a great difference in interest payments from 1996 levels, while for Giuliano Gasparini at independent research group Prometeia "(lower) interest payments continue to have a positive effect but not more than 1.0 trillion lire."
Credito estimated interest charges at 13.0 trillion this month from 14.2 trillion a year ago, saying: "The last mini rise in rates market rates had a slightly negative effect."

Gasparini said unforeseen local authority spending had a negative effect while the new Euro-tax, imposed in March to help Italy reach criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU), numbered among the positive factors.

Analysts said state borrowing for all 1997 would benefit from the latest mini-budget which should cut the year's budget deficit to just above three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), the magic ratio for joining EMU.
Economists were doubtful the mini-budget would bring all the 15.5 trillion lire of deficit cutting benefits the government expects, with Capretti estimating a real effect of 14.0 trillion.
"We believe in the big items but we're more puzzled over the extension of the tax amnesty and advance payments on inheritance tax as well as the cut in spending by ministries," he said.

Analysts expected public sector accounts to improve in coming months, helped by the effects of the Eurotax and with the largest impact from the mini-budget kicking in at the end of July and the end of November, when revenue from an advance tax on employees' severance pay will come due.
But the level of interest rate charges remained possibly the greatest factor generating uncertainty on the ultimate size of the 1997 deficit, analysts said.

Brokers Caboto said: "Rating the effectiveness of all the corrective measures at 75 percent, the public administration deficit should in any case approach three percent of GDP this year even if there is an agreement to delay the start of EMU."
"Taking account the effects of the corrective measures, we will enter the ballpark area for negotiation over taking part from the start of EMU," said Marco Ricci at Centrosim.
Following is a table of analysts' forecasts (in trillion lire):
